## Table 1

The baseline filter selects one intended row per participant, so repeated visits do not make a participant count several times. `select()` chooses the characteristics to describe and `tbl_summary(by = studyarm)` puts the randomized arms in separate columns. This table describes who entered the comparison; it is not an estimate of treatment benefit. A missing or inapplicable questionnaire score is not a zero score.

`bold_labels()`, captions and `as_flex_table()` change presentation. The [gtsummary tutorial](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/articles/tbl_summary.html) shows how to read and customize the defaults [@gtsummarytutorial]. The script saves it with the other tables at the end.

```{r}
#| label: table-1
#| eval: false
```

## Count outcome summary

This describes the distribution of participant-level counts by arm and stores it as `count_outcome_summary`. Raw counts can differ because follow-up durations differ. Use the [count-model page](04_fit_count_models.qmd) to understand the separate rate comparison that accounts for duration. Model tables are produced by the model scripts, not this descriptive block.

```{r}
#| label: count-outcome-summary
#| eval: false
```

## Export tables

Every table, from this script and the model scripts, is saved to `tables/` as a Word file, one file per table, with [`save_table()`](functions.qmd#save-a-table), which converts gtsummary tables with `as_flex_table()` and saves them with flextable's `save_as_docx()`. The file name says where the table came from, for example `mixed_model_effects_itt_act_score_overall.docx`. `tables/` is not committed: the tables are made from study data and stay private until they are cleared for release.

```{r}
#| label: export-tables
#| eval: false
```
